title: Diagnosing drought–flood vulnerability of rice systems across growth stages using Sentinel-1/2 and CHIRPS time series
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Compound and rapidly alternating drought and flood events pose a major challenge to rice production because crop impacts depend strongly on when hydroclimatic stress occurs and how crop condition evolves afterwards. Here, rice vulnerability is characterized by stage-specific exposure, sensitivity, and recovery. We developed a Stage-resolved Drought–flood Rice Vulnerability (SDRV) framework to diagnose vulnerability formation in stable single-season rice across the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River (MLYR), China, during 2020–2025. SDRV integrates CHIRPS precipitation and Sentinel-1/2 time-series within four regionally harmonized growth-stage windows: establishment to early tillering (S1), tillering to jointing (S2), booting/heading to grain filling (S3), and grain filling to maturity (S4). Stage-specific percentile mapping places the underlying hydroclimatic and canopy observations in a common 0–1 diagnostic space, after which the three components are integrated into stage-wise and annual vulnerability. Results show that annual vulnerability ranked as 2022 > 2025 > 2023 > 2020 > 2021 > 2024. Within the study period, drought-dominant and drought-involved pathways were associated with greater annual vulnerability than the flood-dominant pathway represented by 2020. Vulnerability amplification was concentrated mainly in S2–S3. In 2022, persistent drought-dominant stress intensified vulnerability toward S3, producing the highest annual mean vulnerability (0.599) and the largest high-vulnerability fraction (50.4%). In 2025, alternating drought and flood conditions generated a different pathway, with vulnerability concentrated in S2 and partially reduced in S3. Spatially, high vulnerability repeatedly formed a northern and central MLYR corridor, especially across Anhui, Jiangsu and adjoining parts of the middle Yangtze region. Province-level comparison with a yield-loss proxy further showed a positive external-consistency relationship for annual vulnerability after accounting for year effects. These results demonstrate that rice vulnerability under drought–flood stress develops through stage-dependent interactions among hydroclimatic forcing, canopy response, and subsequent recovery. SDRV therefore provides a process-oriented approach for identifying when and where vulnerability intensifies within the growing season.

title: Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water quality retrieval in Poyang Lake using Sentinel-2 imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Accurate retrieval of water-quality parameters from remote-sensing imagery is essential for monitoring large inland lakes, yet pronounced spatial heterogeneity and limited transferability across varying environmental conditions remain major challenges. This study proposes a Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water-quality retrieval from Sentinel-2 imagery in Poyang Lake. PISA-Net integrates a CNN branch for nonlinear spectral–spatial feature learning with a knowledge-guided branch based on empirical optical descriptors and coordinate-derived geographic priors. A geographic soft-assignment mechanism constructs the spatial prior vector, which conditions CNN features through Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), while a stop gradient consistency loss (SG-CL) promotes agreement between the two prediction pathways with controlled gradient propagation. Chl-a, TP, and CODMn were modeled independently and evaluated using 5-fold spatial-block cross-validation against six representative empirical, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning baselines. PISA-Net achieved R 2 values of 0.6113, 0.5112, and 0.5054 for Chl-a, TP, and CODMn, respectively, consistently outperforming the strongest baseline, 2D-CNN, while reducing RMSE by approximately 29.6%, 21.4%, and 19.0%. An additional April 2018 cross-season experiment revealed substantial degradation under direct zero-shot transfer, whereas few-shot adaptation markedly reduced prediction errors, indicating useful cross-season adaptability after limited local calibration. Overall, PISA-Net provides a prior-informed spectral–spatial framework for water-quality retrieval under spatially heterogeneous conditions, while broader multi-season validation remains necessary to establish comprehensive seasonal generalizability.

title: Developing broadband spectral index for estimating crop canopy water content
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Transforming Leaf-Off LiDAR to leaf-on canopy height models using deep learning
abstract: Accurate tree canopy metrics are essential for a wide range of ecological, environmental, and climate studies. Recent advances in airborne LiDAR sensing have greatly expanded access to high-resolution three-dimensional observations of tree canopy structure. However, many widely available airborne LiDAR datasets are acquired under leaf-off conditions to support terrain mapping, and our analysis across ecologically diverse sites shows that canopy height models (CHMs) derived from these data exhibit substantial, recurring discrepancies in canopy height and extent, with an overall tendency to underrepresent canopy structure relative to leaf-on conditions. These discrepancies limit the direct use of leaf-off CHMs in applications requiring canopy information representative of leaf-on conditions. To address this limitation, we introduce a deep learning framework for reconstructing leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs. To our knowledge, this is the first study to formulate the direct reconstruction of leaf-on CHMs from existing leaf-off LiDAR-derived CHMs as a supervised image-to-image learning task. The framework provides two complementary models: a Pix2Pix model that uses the leaf-off CHM alone and a U-Net model that additionally incorporates multispectral imagery. Our proposed models achieve robust canopy-height accuracy across four spatially independent test sites (R²: 0.85–0.92; Mean Absolute Error: 1.3–1.6 metres), substantially reducing the discrepancies observed in the leaf-off source CHMs. They also provide sharper delineation of canopy details and higher accuracy than recent optical-imagery-based approaches. To facilitate broader use, we developed an open-access web application that deploys the pre-trained models and supports on-demand leaf-on CHM generation for user-selected areas across the U.S. where suitable leaf-off LiDAR inputs are available. Overall, the framework provides a practical means to bridge the seasonal data gap in LiDAR acquisition and improve access to reliable canopy metrics representative of leaf-on conditions.

title: Efficient Time-Fractional Diffusion Network for Under-Display ToF Imaging and Beyond
CorrCLIPv2: Harnessing Unlabeled Images for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
Cross-view guided remote sensing super-resolution via constrained residual refinement
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Existing RSISR reconstructs high-resolution imagery primarily from the degraded satellite observation, leaving missing fine-scale information underconstrained. We study whether geo-associated but geometrically misaligned ground imagery can provide useful auxiliary information for satellite super-resolution. We formulate Cross-View Guided Super-Resolution (CVG-SR) and propose Selective Residual Constrained Guidance (SRCG), which restricts ground-derived guidance to gated residual refinement around a satellite-conditioned reconstruction anchor. On VIGOR, matched ground guidance improves PSNR by 1.79 dB over the reconstruction anchor under realistic degradation and also outperforms fine-tuned satellite-only baselines. The advantage persists across higher magnification, different reconstruction anchors, and alternative guidance representations, while external-domain evaluations show that the effect remains observable under domain shift. The source code is available at https://github.com/zqluo-buaa/CVG-SR .

title: Passive microwave sea ice concentration biases in the Southern Hemisphere revealed by ICESat-2 linear ice fraction
abstract: Gridded sea ice concentration (SIC) data are fundamental for understanding long-term polar climate. Since 1978, daily SIC data have been derived from passive microwave (PM) satellite observations. As SIC is not directly observed, it is obtained through an algorithmic inversion of PM brightness temperatures. Differences between PM-SIC algorithms lead to uncertainty in SIC data. Here we examine differences between several PM-SIC products and focus primarily on two: the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) Climate Data Record (CDR), which over our study period is derived from Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS) data, and over the Southern Ocean is largely based on the Bootstrap (BT) PM-SIC algorithm, and the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2)-based NASATeam2 (NT2) product. On individual days, changes in integrated Antarctic sea ice area (SIA) can reach as high as 1.6 million km 2 in summer with relative differences up to 37% at the annual sea ice minimum. Using more than 1.8 million coincident observations of the ICESat-2 Linear Ice Fraction (LIF) from 2018 to 2024, we find BT-based PM-SIC data underestimate Antarctic SIC by a median of 0.2 in areas classified as the marginal ice zone (MIZ), corresponding to a median relative difference in SIC of 31%. This offset is seasonally, spatially, and parametrically consistent and yields differences in apparent MIZ extent as high as 4.4 million km 2 . The offset exceeds reported CDR uncertainties that average 0.07 and cannot be explained as a consequence of sensor differences. The parametric simplicity of the observed bias means these offsets can be parameterized as a function of BT SIC alone, which could lead to an improved SIC dataset for Antarctic studies.

title: A revised model for atmospheric adjacency effect correction in optical satellite earth observation images
RT-ProtoNet: radiative-transfer-guided few-shot prototype networks for cross-region bathymetry in optically clear reef environments
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry faces two coupled obstacles: labels are scarce, and models transfer poorly across regions. We propose RT-ProtoNet, a radiative-transfer-guided few-shot prototype network, which takes patches from three penetrating Sentinel-2 bands and treats ICESat-2 depths, aggregated to the 10 m grid, as sparse supervision; cross-region episodic meta-training then yields a transferable metric representation. Rather than embedding the radiative transfer relation as an analytic formula, we use it as a comparability criterion between support and query pixels, entering the attention as a learnable additive distance penalty. The prediction sums a convex combination over support depths and a base regression head trained on source domains only and frozen at deployment, so no target-domain parameters are estimated. We evaluate on five optically clear shallow reef regions by leave-one-region-out cross-validation against airborne laser bathymetry, against nine baselines, where K is the total number of support pixels (3, 5, 10, 20, 50). For K ≤ 20, RT-ProtoNet attains the lowest cross-region macro-mean RMSE (2.79–2.48 m), with a run-to-run standard deviation 0.67 times the runner-up’s; at K = 50, pre-training with head fine-tuning overtakes it. Ablation shows the residual head’s gain scales with support depth coverage (correlation 0.991) and that the two physical priors are largely substitutable; twelve perturbations to the attenuation input change RMSE by only 0.66%. The method suits depths of roughly 2–20 m and budgets of K ≤ 20, and does not extrapolate to turbid or optically complex waters. Independent evaluation at two external optical-domain sites, a moderately turbid embayment (Tampa Bay) and a clear-to-moderately-turbid transition site (Boquerón Bay), further delineates the method’s applicability across contrasting optical conditions, showing reliable transfer within the clear-water regime but substantial degradation under stronger optical attenuation.

title: UrbanQGS: Large-scale urban surface reconstruction via analytic curvature consistency in quadratic Gaussian splatting
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Large-scale 3D surface reconstruction at the city scale from UAV imagery is a core task for building digital-twin cities. Although 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and its variants have achieved remarkable progress in radiance-field reconstruction, existing methods still struggle with scale-varying structural complexity and diverse urban textures: geometry is often incomplete in low-frequency, weak-texture regions over large areas, while in high-frequency regions with intricate details, disordered primitive distributions tend to cause floating artifacts and outliers. To address these issues, we propose UrbanQGS, a large-scale urban reconstruction framework built on quadratic Gaussian splatting. We inherit quadratic surface Gaussians as scene primitives and use their analytic curvature as the central driving signal to perform a two-stage geometric refinement: (1) A self-supervised geometric constraint based on cross-view curvature consistency, which effectively fills geometric holes in weak-texture planar regions. (2) A curvature-aware adaptive representation allocation strategy that reweights, recalibrates, and ranks densification gradients, guiding split and clone operations toward geometrically complex regions while standard pruning removes redundant primitives. In addition, we integrate a monocular normal prior to correct global orientation drift during large-scale reconstruction. We further assess the compatibility of UrbanQGS with partitioned large-scene reconstruction using a visibility-aware block-wise protocol with hardware-constrained per-block budgets. The blocks are trained sequentially on a single GPU. Experiments on large-scale UAV datasets demonstrate that, compared with state-of-the-art 3DGS-based large-scale reconstruction methods, UrbanQGS maintains superior geometric quality while substantially reducing redundant Gaussians and mesh complexity, yielding finer and more complete geometric structures, while qualitative results on our custom-collected dataset indicate its compatibility with a partitioned large-scene reconstruction pipeline.

title: N-PCLN: A physics-informed deep learning framework for short-term chlorophyll-a prediction with sparse satellite observation
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Chlorophyll-a (Chla) is a key indicator of lake eutrophication. Its short-term prediction is essential for water quality monitoring and bloom early warning. However, traditional deep learning models often rely heavily on dense observations and provide limited process interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a physics-informed deep learning framework, named N-PCLN, for short-term Chla prediction in Erhai Lake. The framework integrates Sentinel-3 OLCI imagery and meteorological datasets from 2016 to 2024. It uses Chla, land surface temperature, wind speed, and precipitation as inputs. Total phosphorus is incorporated through a nutrient–phytoplankton model to construct a physical loss. This design enables the model to jointly learn spatiotemporal patterns and nutrient–phytoplankton process constraints. The N-PCLN outperforms ConvLSTM, Transformer, MDN, CNN, and LSTM models, achieving an R 2 of 0.767, an MAE of 1.483 mg/m 3 , and an RMSE of 2.665 mg/m 3 . Sparse-data experiments show that N-PCLN maintains more stable performance than the selected baseline models under reduced data availability. The ablation experiments indicate that LST is the dominant meteorological factor driver of short-term Chla dynamics, while wind speed and precipitation mainly affect hydrodynamic redistribution and runoff-related nutrient transport. Physical-loss gradient analysis further reveals that the N-P constraint acts differently across seasons and Chla concentration. These results demonstrate that N-PCLN improves both prediction performance and process interpretability. It provides a useful framework for satellite-based lake water quality prediction.

title: Assessing the spatio-temporal cumulative drought effects on two Mediterranean forest types in Central Chile
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Droughts are long-lasting events that can drive persistent functional changes in ecosystems, particularly in drought-prone areas like Mediterranean forests. We integrated a phenology-based anomaly method, combining kernel density estimation (KDE) with cumulative sums (CUSUMs) to assess long-term drought impacts on two Mediterranean forest types in Central Chile. Using MODIS Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), the Moisture Stress Index (MSI), and Evapotranspiration (ET) from 2000 to 2024, we quantified cumulative deviations in canopy productivity, moisture conditions, and energy exchange. Our framework revealed persistent negative functional trajectories preceding the well-documented 2010–present megadrought. Spatially explicit metrics identified coherent degradation hotspots in northern sclerophyllous and southern deciduous forests, where canopy greenness, moisture, and evapotranspiration declined synchronously. Seasonal models indicated a post-2010 strengthening of soil–water controls over forest functioning, with soil moisture and water storage variables becoming influential predictors. The convergence of cumulative negative EVI, MSI, and ET signals highlights widespread and sustained functional weakening under prolonged drought conditions. Our results demonstrate that integrating KDE-derived anomalies with cumulative deviation tracking provides a sensitive and transferable framework to detect early and persistent vegetation stress in water-limited ecosystems.

title: Deep learning detection of submesoscale eddies from MODIS SST in the South China Sea
abstract: Submesoscale eddies play crucial roles in oceanic energy cascades and material transport; however, their detection faces substantial challenges owing to inadequate spatial resolution in traditional satellite altimetric measurements. This research introduces Sub-Eddy-Net, an innovative deep learning approach utilizing an enhanced YOLOv8-SGAM architecture for identifying submesoscale eddy features within MODIS-derived sea surface temperature (SST) imagery across the South China Sea region. By exploiting SST data's advantageous temporal coverage and observational continuity relative to altimetric sensors, synthetic aperture radar, and ocean color products, the developed algorithm demonstrates detection precision of 0.968, successfully identifying 20,443 submesoscale eddies throughout 2015–2024. Results indicate cyclonic eddy prevalence exceeds anticyclonic occurrences, exhibiting average radii of 13.1 km and 13.7 km respectively. Eddy distributions primarily cluster within coastal waters and Luzon Strait vicinity, displaying pronounced seasonal patterns. Comparison with Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) observations shows 64.3% matched features, 27.1% positional offsets, and 8.6% detected only in SST. Within the same eddies, coherent chlorophyll-a (Chla) signatures were present in a smaller fraction, indicating that SST is the more robust tracer for systematic detection. This Sub-Eddy-Net methodology offers a scalable approach for examining submesoscale oceanic phenomena, providing a decadal inventory for further study of their roles in ocean circulation and vertical exchange.

title: Unsupervised Clustering of Public Transport Vehicles Using Deep Morphological Features and Color Histograms
abstract: Surveillance cameras along urban roads produce large volumes of unlabeled video that could support the monitoring of public transport, but grouping the observed vehicles into meaningful categories without manual annotation remains challenging, since buses from different routes often share the same body structure and differ mainly in their color schemes. This study presents an unsupervised clustering methodology for public transport vehicles that combines morphological features extracted with a frozen DINOv2 Vision Transformer and handcrafted HSV color histograms through weighted early fusion, followed by UMAP projection and K-Means clustering. The method was evaluated on 7,972 bus images extracted from about 1,460 hours of video of an arterial road in Mexico City, with the goal of isolating the buses of the city's public bus network (RTP) without supervision. With a fusion of 65\% morphological and 35\% color features, the pipeline produced 14 clusters that separate distinct routes and vehicle types, and it increased the precision of the target cluster with respect to morphological features alone. These results show that color complements self-supervised features for route-level clustering, provided that it does not dominate the representation.

title: Safe and Fuel-Efficient Motion Planning for Lunar Propulsive Drones
abstract: Propulsive drones are a promising new technology for generating high-resolution terrain models of the Moon. In future lunar missions, propulsive drones will complete a series of hops across the lunar surface while capturing images with downward-facing cameras. We present an autonomous motion planning framework that uses a vision-guided optimal control strategy for performing safe, efficient hops between specified waypoints. The drone plans parabolic hops between waypoints generated by a global-level planner; if a nominal waypoint is unsafe or unreachable, the drone then completes a diversion maneuver to safely land. To evaluate the validity of potential landing sites, we develop a custom semantic segmentation model for identifying obstacles from aerial images, and we introduce an approach for rapidly calculating reachable terrain. We then use model predictive control (MPC) to robustly track hop trajectories that guide the drone towards safe landing sites. We test the optimal hop planner in a high-fidelity lunar simulation environment. Our results demonstrate that our unified motion planning framework yields safe, fuel-efficient hop trajectories which can be tracked rapidly and with low error via MPC.

title: Data-Efficient ConvNeXt Pretraining for High-Resolution Sentinel-1 GRD SAR Representation Learning
abstract: Labeled Sentinel-1 Ground Range Detected (S1GRD) datasets remain scarce, limiting supervised deep learning for land-surface remote sensing, while self-supervised pretraining for this domain has been dominated by Vision Transformer (ViT)-based masked image modeling requiring substantial data and compute. We propose SparK-SAR, a sparse convolutional masked pretraining framework built on SparK and ConvNeXt, designed to exploit convolutional inductive biases for S1GRD imagery under constrained compute. SparK-SAR makes three core technical contributions: (i) ConvNeXt-RS, a domain-adapted encoder that halves the stem stride (4x to 2x) to produce 14x14 feature maps at stride 16x, providing 4x more spatial tokens at identical parameter count; (ii) a lightweight ConvNeXt-512 reconstruction decoder with PixelShuffle upsampling that reduces pretraining VRAM by 7.5-8.5% per GPU relative to a UNet-128 baseline while matching its accuracy; and (iii) an empirical characterization of FP16 mixed-precision pretraining instability in the standard SparK UNet-768 decoder on S1GRD data, complemented by a finding that finetuning with layer-wise learning rate decay (LLRD) improves downstream performance of pretrained encoders. On four Copernicus-Bench S1GRD tasks, our finetuned 27.8M-parameter ConvNeXt-RS encoder improves over a non-pretrained baseline by +4.7, +5.0, +5.8, and +1.4 pp on EuroSAT-S1, BigEarthNet-S1, DFC2020-S1, and Flood-S1 respectively, and outperforms the Copernicus-FM ViT (139M parameters, frozen) on three of four tasks at roughly 5x fewer parameters. A pretraining data-scaling study reveals task-dependent data efficiency: classification saturates with as little as 10-25% of the SSL4EO-S12 v1.1 corpus, while dense prediction continues to improve significantly up to 25-50%. The study also includes a CKA representation analysis and a geographic de-collision experiment.

title: VesperMUSE: Multi-Modal Fusion Vision Transformer for Image Semantic Segmentation Under Diverse Light Conditions
abstract: Semantic segmentation is critical for the reliable navigation and scene understanding of autonomous systems, yet its performance degrades severely in low-light environments due to noise, artifacts, colour distortion, and the loss of structural details. To address this challenge, this work introduces VesperMUSE, a unified multi-modal framework designed to achieve robust image semantic segmentation across diverse illumination conditions. The architecture addresses the light deficiency problem on multiple levels: proposing a novel physics-informed synthetic low-light adaptation algorithm, approaching Low-Light Image Enhancement (LLIE) through a thermal-guided paradigm, and finally aiming to recover the intrinsic scene details for semantic segmentation through a multi-modal fusion approach. Following enhancement, the framework dynamically integrates the primary RGB features with auxiliary thermal representations and surface normal maps highlighting geometric discontinuities and material boundaries. At the core of this integration is a highly scalable, modality-agnostic self-attention mechanism that extracts both global context and fine local features from an arbitrary number of auxiliary inputs. By combining and projecting these hierarchical multi-modal representations into a unified component, the attention module allows the network to selectively attend to relevant cross-modal cues without requiring any architectural modifications when different sensor configurations are used. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that VesperMUSE successfully recovers missing visual cues, providing a flexible, state-of-the-art (SOTA) solution for machine perception in extreme and unstructured real-world environments.

title: Self-Calibrated Subspace Robust PCA for Parameter-Free Removal of Mixed Noise and Line Stripes in Hyperspectral Images
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) are often corrupted by Gaussian noise, impulses and stripes whose intensities vary across bands. The representative coefficient correlated total variation (RCCTV) model restores HSIs efficiently, but it lacks Gaussian and stripe terms, and its noise-aware extensions require the noise level and a stripe budget to be specified in advance. This article proposes a self-calibrated RCCTV (SC-RCCTV) model, in which the noise parameters are estimated adaptively during the iterations. A band-wise dense term and line-constant column and row stripe terms are introduced into RCCTV. The noise level of each band is initialized by a stripe-invariant median absolute deviation estimator and refined online from the residual, which turns the separation of sparse and dense noise into a band-adaptive Huber loss, and the stripe thresholds follow from a significance test whose false-alarm rate can be predicted analytically. No parameter is tuned for a specific image, and every subproblem of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) solver is solved in closed form. Under line stripes, SC-RCCTV outperforms the parameter-free FastHyMix by 8.17 dB on native-size cubes, and, without any noise information, it exceeds S3TTV, which is given the true noise parameters, by 1.52 dB while running more than 1,900 times faster. On average, it stays within 0.01 dB of the same model given the true noise levels, and its online calibration improves on a two-stage estimate-then-denoise scheme. Experiments on real Indian Pines and Urban data further delineate its scope for stripes that do not span entire lines.

title: FuseAdapt: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Fusion for Semantic Segmentation with Missing Modalities
abstract: Multi-modal semantic segmentation benefits from complementary sensors, but this benefit is fragile when some modalities are degraded or missing at test time. Many existing methods rely on dedicated fusion modules or multi-branch cross-modal encoders, and the fusion often becomes unreliable when modalities are absent, leading to substantial performance drops. We propose \textbf{FuseAdapt}, a parameter-efficient framework that performs fusion within the adaptation space of a frozen vision foundation model (VFM), exploring whether VFM priors can serve as an effective shared backbone for multi-modal segmentation. Instead of attaching a standalone fusion network, FuseAdapt assigns each modality a lightweight adaptation branch and performs \emph{adaptation-space fusion} by keeping Q/V low-rank adaptation private to each modality and routing only FFN low-rank residual activations across modalities inside the frozen backbone. The pretrained VFM remains fixed while modality-specific corrections and explicit cross-modal interaction are learned through the adaptation paths. To handle missing modalities, we further introduce \textbf{Predictive Modality Modeling (PMM)}, a direct representation-level objective for cross-modal redundancy. During training, PMM masks a target modality and predicts its embedding from the visible ones, supervised by a teacher target computed under full-modality input. PMM is used only during training and adds no inference-time overhead. Across three multi-modal segmentation benchmarks (MCubeS, DELIVER, MUSES), FuseAdapt consistently improves both modality-complete and modality-incomplete segmentation with a small trainable budget, yielding up to +3.01 mIoU under full modalities and +12.56 mIoU under missing modalities over prior state-of-the-art. Project page: https://devinxzhang.github.io/FuseAdapt-Page/.

title: SCMerge: Spatial-Consistency-Aware Token Pair Merging for Efficient Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Vision Transformer architectures have showcased impressive performance on semantic segmentation, yet their quadratic attention complexity hinders practical applications. Recent works have focused on merging tokens to reduce sequence length and thus improve transformer efficiency. However, existing token merging methods primarily rely on feature similarity to identify similar tokens, overlooking spatial consistency, which may introduce segmentation errors in semantic segmentation. In this work, we propose SCMerge, a training-free token merging method that jointly considers feature similarity and spatial consistency in pairing similar tokens. The pairwise tokens are then merged within the encoder, and the resulting token sequences are reconstructed onto the original patch grid after decoding. The proposed method is flexible and can be plugged into existing vision Transformer-based semantic segmentation pipelines. Extensive experiments on the benchmark datasets ADE20K, Pascal Context, and Cityscapes show that SCMerge consistently achieves a better trade-off between segmentation accuracy and efficiency than baseline methods.

title: Spurious Attention Heads in Vision Transformers: Mechanistic Identification of Annotation-Driven Bias in Medical Chest X-Ray Analysis
abstract: Vision Transformers deployed in medical imaging exploit spurious correlations, yet the internal mechanisms remain unidentified and impossible to fix. We apply mechanistic interpretability to locate one such mechanism in ViT-Base 16: a single attention head (L8H10) that functions as a dedicated annotation-reader on chest X-rays, attending to corner text rather than lung pathology in 62% of 200 COVID-19 images. Causal validation via inpainting confirms annotation content rather than luminance or edge density drives the behaviour, increasing lung attention 1.52 times upon removal in affected images ($p{<}0.0001$). The finding replicates across NIH ChestX-ray14 (79%), DeiT-Base (88%), and ViT-Large 16 (80%), establishing spurious annotation-attending heads as a consistent property of ViT-family architectures across two datasets and three architectures. Full fine-tuning does not suppress the behaviour and may entrench it: 98.4% of spurious images remain spurious and the spurious rate rises marginally, as the shortcut is reinforced rather than removed. Critically, single-head ablation produces $p{=}0.340$ and multi-head ablation of all three identified carriers produces $p{=}0.532$, meaning a causally verified annotation-reading circuit is completely invisible to output-level evaluation. Mechanistic auditing finds what behavioural testing cannot.

title: When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark
abstract: Muon's gains in data efficiency motivate evaluating its performance under explicit data, time, and tuning budgets. On a single A100 GPU, we compare a reference single-device Muon implementation with AdamW across 17.7M- and 33.6M-parameter causal language models and 2.70M-parameter vision transformers. A common 23-candidate development budget selects configurations evaluated with five matched seeds, full validation trajectories, optimizer-step timing, and a frozen one-shot test. Muon reduces validation-loss area under the curve by 3.25--22.44\% at equal data and lowers test loss in all 20 primary pairs. In this configuration, Muon improves time-normalized loss area} by 19.68--22.31\% on vision, while AdamW is better by 3.38--6.96\% on language. The full Muon optimizer call, including auxiliary AdamW updates, consumes 56.1--69.6\% of training time, compared with 6.1--9.1\% for the AdamW baseline. Muon also has higher expected regret under restricted access to these candidate pools. These results characterize small models with reference kernels; their wall-clock ordering does not establish a ranking for larger models or optimized implementations.

title: ISW-Agent: Integrating LLM-Driven Dialogue with n8n Workflow for Internal Solitary Wave Remote Sensing Image Processing
abstract: Internal solitary wave (ISW) remote sensing requires task parameters and spatial information to be transferred across image acquisition, detection, stripe extraction, and propagation prediction. Here, we present ISW-Agent, which integrates large language model (LLM) interpretation with n8n workflows and independent scientific models through structured task constraints, geospatial transformations, and stage-specific output validation. In tests of 120 Chinese instructions per backend, GPT-5.6 Sol and DeepSeek both achieved a strict task-match rate of 94.2%, with all intents and execution decisions matching the reference. Sentinel-1 cases demonstrated continuous processing from dialogue requests to wavefront prediction for the specified scene. Of 50 timed scenes, 39 completed detection, extraction, and prediction with a median turnaround time of 48.04 s; 11 stopped after empty extraction. Across 3,408 controlled fault-injection runs, retries recovered 234 transient-failure conditions and output validation rejected 234 structural defects, while 61 provenance or completeness errors indicated the need for content-consistency checks. Overall, ISW-Agent thus connects natural-language requests to traceable spatial processing chains for multimodel ISW analysis.

title: Where, How, and When: Query-Guided Grounding for Video Understanding
abstract: Understanding video content requires reasoning at multiple levels of granularity, from identifying objects to interpreting their interactions and localizing when specific actions occur. This thesis studies three query-guided grounding tasks that answer where key objects are (object-level grounding), how they interact (relationship-level grounding), and when specific moments occur (moment-level grounding). For object-level grounding, we present QDETRv, a query-guided extension of the Detection Transformer for one-shot localization of unseen objects in videos, which combines query-context fusion, a memory module for temporal consistency, and unsupervised pretraining on synthetic object trajectories. We further propose the Temporal Object-Aware Vision Transformer (TOViT) for few-shot video object detection, which builds on a language-aligned open-set vision encoder and propagates high-confidence object features across frames. For relationship-level grounding, we introduce few-shot referring relationships in videos: given a (subject, predicate, object) query and a few support videos sharing the predicate, the entities are localized by optimizing a T-partite random field using a meta-learned relation network with query-conditioned translational embeddings, Global Semantic Aggregation, Local Localization Aggregation, and belief-propagation-based message passing. For moment-level grounding, we propose the Moment Alignment Transformer (MATR) for video-to-video moment retrieval, which uses dual-stage Dynamic Time Warping for pre- and post-fusion alignment, learnable queries for boundary prediction, and self-supervised pretraining with temporal augmentations; MATR also extends to text-to-video moment retrieval with performance comparable to, or better than, the state of the art. These contributions advance query-guided video understanding across spatial, relational, and temporal grounding.

title: CoViG: Coarsened Vision GNN for Image Classification
abstract: Although Graph Neural Networks are widely used in various domains, they remained mostly unexplored in computer vision. Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers were leading the field, until the quite recent introduction of Vision Graphs (ViG) that treat images as a set of nodes and apply graph convolution on their k-NN graphs. ViGs show impressive accuracy on image classification but their computational cost remains relatively high. Inspired by optimization methods for GNNs, we present CoViG, a novel approach combining graph coarsening and ViGs. Our method introduces an additional MinCUT pooling step within the Grapher component of intermediate ViG blocks. By simplifying the intermediate graphs and thus decreasing the number of nodes of specific blocks, our approach considerably reduces the computational cost of ViG during inference. We evaluated our approach on ImageNet with several ViG architectures, and we obtained accuracies equivalent to the original ViG models with only about 51\% of FLOPs.

title: A large-scale climate-aware satellite image dataset for domain adaptive land-cover semantic segmentation
abstract: A few well-annotated datasets for land-cover semantic segmentation have recently been introduced to advance the field of earth observation technologies. However, these datasets overlook the significant diversity among geographic areas with different climates, which can greatly impact and diversify land cover. Consequently, this leads to a domain gap in remote sensing images and severe performance degradation of the segmentation models. To enhance land-cover semantic segmentation with improved generalization ability, we conducted the first investigation into the impact of climate on this task. In this paper, we present a unique large-scale Climate-Aware Satellite Images Dataset (CASID) specifically designed for domain adaptive land-cover semantic segmentation. It consists of 980 satellite images with a size of 5000 x 5000 pixels, collected from 30 different regions around Asia, covering over 24,500 square kilometers. These images are gathered from four distinct climate zones, namely temperate monsoon, subtropical monsoon, tropical monsoon, and tropical rainforest. It includes four sub-datasets/domains, each representing one of the aforementioned climate zones. This characteristic makes CASID the first climate-aware land-cover semantic segmentation dataset with multiple domains. Additionally, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the samples from the four climate zones, emphasizing differences in global image features, image texture, category distribution, spectral value, and object shape. These analyses offer valuable insights for subsequent research in this field. Moreover, we conduct extensive experiments to evaluate the latest semantic segmentation and unsupervised domain adaptation methods on the CASID dataset. These results serve as a robust baseline for future research endeavors. Our dataset will be made publicly available at https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/CASID.

title: Vision-Guided Closed-Loop Autonomous Navigation of Light-Driven Janus Microbots
abstract: Artificial microbots capable of precise and autonomous navigation could provide versatile platforms for microscale transport, manipulation, and task execution in complex environments. However, reliable navigation becomes increasingly challenging at the micrometre scale, particularly when the surrounding environment changes dynamically. Here, we develop a vision-guided closed-loop navigation framework for light-driven cube-shaped hematite/TiO2 Janus microbots with a characteristic size of approximately 3 μm. Real-time visual localization using a custom-trained YOLOv11 object-detection model is integrated with discretized waypoint-based magnetic steering to enable precise navigation along complex prescribed trajectories, with more than 90% of the measured trajectory deviations remaining below 6 μm across the tested path geometries. The framework further enables arbitrary user-defined free-hand trajectories and autonomous navigation through a physically confined maze. In dynamically changing environments, A* path planning enables real-time path replanning while avoiding multiple independently swimming 5 μm spherical Janus micromotors. Finally, the microbot selectively captures multiple cargo particles and autonomously transports and delivers them to a predefined location while simultaneously avoiding dynamic obstacles. These results establish an integrated platform combining programmable trajectory control, autonomous path planning, real-time environmental adaptation, and task execution within a single light-driven Janus microbot system.

title: SpaceCache: Intermediate Feature Reuse for Efficient Semantic Segmentation on Point Cloud Streams
abstract: Point-cloud streams are central to autonomous driving and robotics, yet existing segmentation networks process every frame from scratch, although consecutive frames largely overlap. We observe that the intermediate features of point-cloud transformers remain semantically consistent across frames for the same spatial region, especially in deep stages. Building on this, we present SpaceCache, a training-free feature cache that reuses these features across frames. Tokens of previously observed regions skip a sequence of transformer blocks and take their cached features, only the remaining tokens are computed, and the full token layout is restored for dense prediction. Lightweight cache management keeps reused features reliable by limiting each entry's age and evicting low-confidence entries. Unlike token merging, SpaceCache selects tokens at negligible cost and runs its cache operations once per encoder stage. On both outdoor and indoor benchmarks, such as nuScenes, Waymo, and ScanNet, with two transformer backbones of Utonia and LitePT-B, SpaceCache achieves up to 1.65x speedup with less than 1-point mIoU drop and consistently outperforms token-merging methods.

title: Evidence Field for Histopathology: Cross-Centre Evaluation and Replayable Spatial Decisions
abstract: Histopathology classifiers must transfer across acquisition sites while exposing evidence that can be checked independently. Evidence Field couples learned image measurements and spatial classification with a native covering-program record. We evaluate this architecture on all 455,954 released CAMELYON17-WILDS patches, using patient-separated source partitions and two held-out hospital centres. Eighteen from-scratch fits compare four Evidence Field objectives with residual convolutional and compact vision-transformer classifiers. Checkpoints, temperatures and review thresholds are selected using source validation. The source-selected paired-cross-entropy ensemble achieves areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.9356 and 0.9453, with accuracies of 84.46% and 86.77% at the two held-out centres. Corresponding convolutional values are 0.7352 and 0.7656, and transformer values are 0.8502 and 0.7924. Evidence Field has 10,550 trainable parameters per member and additionally returns selected covers, signed region and interaction terms, contextual dependencies and independently reconstructible predictions. Patient-cluster intervals, calibration, source-fixed review policies and recorded training resources characterize the results. A 340-image, three-member audit reconstructs probability mixtures and 6,120 class programs under three rigid views. The evaluation supports cross-centre discrimination and reproducible computation for these implemented models; unequal family tuning, previously examined public targets and limited patient groups constrain broader interpretation.

title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
abstract: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of video generative pretraining for unified 4D perception. See https://gen4p.github.io for more visual results.

title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
abstract: Token merging has emerged as an effective training-free strategy for accelerating diffusion models by reducing redundant token computation while minimizing generation degradation. A key challenge is determining which tokens can be safely merged and which should be preserved for subsequent computation. Existing method addresses this by preserving prompt-aligned foreground regions, thereby protecting semantically relevant structures. However, this text-relevance criterion overlooks background objects, local details that are not explicitly mentioned in the prompt, leading to degraded structural coherence. In this work, we propose Dynamics-aware Token Merging (DaTMe), a training-free framework that grounds token merging in the underlying diffusion dynamics. Our key insight is that token importance should reflect whether a token remains unresolved during denoising and whether it carries structural information. To this end, DaTMe constructs a dynamics- aware importance map from the Tweedie denoised estimate. The map combines a temporal signal, measuring inter-step changes in the predicted clean image, with a structural signal, capturing local high-frequency content such as boundaries and fine details. Using this map, DaTMe adaptively assigns tokens into merging roles under a given compression ratio: important tokens are preserved as anchors, while tokens that are both temporally stabilized and structurally homogeneous are selected as safe merge candidates. Experiments on PixArt-a and FLUX demonstrate that DaTMe maintains visual fidelity across the entire image, highlighting diffusion dynamics as an effective token-level merging decision in efficient generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/SeungJuCha/DaTMe.

title: SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. Dynamic caching methods decide when to refresh by accumulating a cheap probe of the network input into a staleness signal and spending a fresh evaluation once it crosses a threshold. They perform hard caching: the signal is a binary switch between refresh and reuse, and every step, fresh or cached, advances by the prescribed step size. We observe that the signal carries much more than this switch. How far it sits below the threshold, its headroom, predicts the error induced by reuse. We propose SoftCache, which performs soft caching: instead of a binary switch, the headroom sets how far each cached step goes. Where the headroom is large, the sampler jumps past several scheduled nodes, and as a refresh nears, its steps shrink back toward the original step. These adaptive jumps may land between the scheduled nodes, taking the sampler off its fixed grid. SoftCache requires no training and adds no per-backbone settings: on FLUX for images and on HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 for video, at speedups from $3.5\times$ to $6.9\times$, it is ahead of every baseline on all four fidelity metrics.

title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
abstract: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
abstract: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets, while producing goal-directed manipulation videos with stronger instruction adherence and action progression than video-generation baselines. Project Page: https://p3-wam.pages.dev/

title: Grounding Generative Verification in 3D Content
abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and 3D generation have expanded 3D understanding and synthesis. However, beyond visual fidelity, task-specific correctness grounded in 3D evidence remains a major challenge. We argue that building reliable 3D systems requires not only stronger generation and reasoning, but also verification feedback that identifies unmet requirements and explains their violations, allowing systems to reflect on and refine their outputs. Such feedback must integrate multi-view observations and distinguish genuine inconsistencies from projection-dependent appearances. We make three contributions. First, we introduce 3DVerifierBench, a benchmark spanning 10 tasks that evaluates decisions, rejection explanations, and responses to controlled changes in specifications and candidates. A human study reveals a 21.6 percentage-point gap between humans and the strongest tested model, GPT-6 Astra, while explanation-aware analysis exposes weaknesses in rejection reliability. Second, we analyze verification across fine-grained factual categories, exposing errors in values and target binding. We develop a scalable pipeline combining multi-view fact extraction, controlled 3D editing, and native annotations to produce 14,126 training examples with contradiction explanations and linked counterfactuals. Third, we examine how verification could support 3D generation through candidate selection and recursive refinement. In human-labeled sixteen-candidate pools, oracle selection improves complete factual success from 26.7% to 90.0%. In a separate eight-input study, human-guided recursive refinement satisfies all seven requirements for every input, compared with three under parallel Oracle@8. Together, our benchmark, analysis, and data pipeline establish a foundation for models to reflect on 3D content through reliable verification feedback.

title: DK-VLM: Geometry as Position for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-language models still struggle to understand 3D spatial relations across views and update spatial judgments as the observer moves. A common approach fuses 3D reconstruction features into visual tokens, but aligning these features with pretrained semantic representations remains challenging under limited spatial supervision. We propose DK-VLM with Dual-Kernel Attention, which computes attention from both a visual token's input position and its geometric position in the scene. A semantic kernel retains the pretrained model's native attention and positional encoding, while a separate geometric kernel uses estimated 3D points and camera poses to directly modulate attention through point displacements and relative view transformations. Then, a learned gate fuses their outputs. Geometry thus enters attention as position rather than as fused reconstruction features. We further introduce Reference-Frame Composition (RC) supervision to train the model to update its reference frame across successive judgments. It provides stepwise turn and heading targets derived from verified single-step annotations. Among the compared methods, DK-VLM-8B achieves the highest average score across six spatial benchmarks and the highest overall scores on VSI-Bench (74.33) and ReVSI-32 (58.28). RC supervision further improves multi-step spatial reasoning, while the full model preserves general video understanding. Project page: https://sumuru789.github.io/DK-VLM-website/.

title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
abstract: Single image 3D generation aims to dress a given 3D mesh with relightable materials while faithfully preserving the visual details of a reference image. Existing methods either introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or struggle to preserve fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning. To resolve these challenges, we introduce SUPRA-Tex, built on the principle of decoupling visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion. This division of labor allows the 3D generator, trained on limited 3D data, to focus its capacity on preserving visible evidence and completing unobserved surfaces. Specifically, we first train an MLLM-based image editing model to predict lighting-separated PBR maps in the reference view. We then project these maps onto the visible surface and encode them with the pretrained material VAE encoder into native observation latents that share the generation target's latent space. An interleaved flow transformer holds these latents as fixed, read-only anchors while alternating unobserved-region and full-surface updates to generate complete material latents. This design achieves super-alignment with the reference, delivering What You See Is What You Get fidelity on visible regions and coherent completion on unobserved surfaces. Trained solely on public datasets, SUPRA-Tex achieves SOTA performance in both geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end asset generation, matching or even exceeding leading commercial systems on in-the-wild images. Project page: https://supra-3d.github.io/supratex/

title: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
abstract: Few-step autoregressive video generators enable streaming generation, yet they run every token through the final denoising step, regardless of how much refinement it needs. We find this uniform computation is often unnecessary: many tokens already closely match their eventual full-step outputs in the initial steps, while others require refinement until the end. We introduce Speculative Forcing, a framework that treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts when individual tokens can be safely accepted early. Once accepted, a token is frozen as its final output and undergoes no further denoising, while its cached keys and values remain available as context for the remaining tokens. We explore two alternative verifier designs: a training-free one based on similarity to clean content and stability across steps, and a learned one that reads the frozen generator's intermediate features to estimate each token's remaining gap to its full-step output. Across short-video, long-video, and world generation, Speculative Forcing preserves the quality of full-step sampling while substantially reducing computation. On LongLive, it matches the four-step generator with ~1.7 denoising steps per token, running over 1.5x faster at 41.7 and 37.8 fps. On Lingbot-World 2.0, where camera motion continually changes the visible content, it maintains quality with ~2.5 denoising steps per token and runs 1.35x faster at 24.5 fps.

title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
abstract: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-frame scale alignment. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and generalizes zero-shot to KITTI and nuScenes. Project page: https://hongchang-liu.github.io/GeoState-project-page/

title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
abstract: We introduce 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem that enables coding agents to create editable and verifiable 3D content at scale. 3DCodeVerse comprises large-scale, high-quality datasets of executable 3D code, a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, and practical guidance for 3D coding. First, we construct 3DCodeVerse-2M, a large-scale curated dataset of standalone 3D executable code. We build this corpus by collecting open-source data, converting specialized representations, and generating new programs with coding agents. Each program is packaged with the source files and associated assets required for execution in its declared environment, along with available descriptions and verification records. Second, we develop the 3DCodeVerse Harness, a multi-agent directed acyclic graph framework for generating and refining 3D content. It uses execution checks, spatial measurements, and visual feedback to automatically evaluate and revise generated programs without human feedback during generation. Third, we conduct systematic empirical studies of 3D coding, establishing baselines with fine-tuned open models and deriving practical guidance through component-level analyses of our harness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that fine-tuning on our dataset significantly improves the 3D coding capabilities of open-source models. Notably, our 3DCodeVerse harness achieves a 90% win rate against Claude Design (3D Object) in pairwise human evaluations, when both are utilized by Claude Opus 5.5.

title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning
abstract: Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original training and multi-turn inference. We introduce a training scheme that makes multi-turn image editing stable under this accumulating distribution shift. A key is to force the editor to operate on its own outputs from previous editing turns during training, bringing the principle of Self-Forcing to image editing. The main challenge is that self-generated editing trajectories deviate from ground-truth trajectories, making direct supervision unreliable. We address this challenge through a distillation objective that leverages a teacher image editor to provide a reliable training signal when the model operates on its own previous outputs. We introduce an asymmetric conditioning scheme: while the student performs edits sequentially on its own outputs, the teacher remains anchored to the original clean image and receives a compound editing instruction. Experiments show substantially reduced degradation over long multi-turn sequences while maintaining editing quality and instruction adherence.

title: Dense4D: Pixel-Level 4D Human Correspondence
abstract: Reconstructing human motion in 4D requires identifying the same surface points through articulation, deformation and changes in visibility. We introduce Dense4D, to our knowledge the first feed-forward model dedicated to dense 4D correspondence across the body, clothing and hair from a set of monocular RGB images, without a body template. Trained specifically for human geometry, Dense4D jointly processes person-centred crops with known image-to-crop transforms to predict Human Point Maps (HPMs) and depth for each image. An HPM assigns each person pixel the 3D position of its observed surface point at a common reference time. These maps support amodal correspondence: points hidden in the reference image can be localised from observations in other frames. Matching HPM coordinates across crops establishes correspondence without predicting camera poses or large scene displacements; per-image depth then lifts the matches into 3D tracks. Experiments on real people demonstrate substantially higher tracking accuracy and closer agreement with scanned surfaces than the evaluated baselines. Points from different frames assemble into coherent human geometry in the reference pose, providing visible evidence of consistent dense correspondence through articulation and clothing deformation. Additional qualitative results, videos, and an interactive viewer are available at https://alpguler.com/dense4d.

title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation
abstract: As joint audio-video generation models become more capable, they can generate audio-visual scenes exhibiting three forms of complexity: multi-event composition, multi-layer audio mixture, and asymmetric cross-modal relations. However, current evaluations largely reuse metrics from earlier simple and unidirectional tasks. They typically evaluate an audio-video clip as a whole and rely on simple predefined relations, making them unsuitable for these increasingly complex scenes. We propose an event-centric evaluation framework that disentangles audio and visual events at the event level, analyzes each event independently, cross-validates relations across modalities, and aggregates the judgments into a coarse-to-fine, three-level consistency metric. The metric assesses global narrative harmony, event-level temporal synchronization, and fine-grained attribute alignment, providing a general formulation for audio-video consistency evaluation across diverse generation settings and cross-modal relations. We instantiate the metric as AVC-Reward, a trainable audio-video reward model. To evaluate the agreement between automatic judgments and human perception across generation paradigms and relation complexities, we construct AVC-Benchmark, which is primarily built from diverse positive and negative samples generated by various types of audio-video generation models. AVC-Reward achieves state-of-the-art alignment with human judgment among automatic methods, provides interpretable rationales that localize failures, and improves the audio-video consistency of a joint generation model when used as an online reinforcement-learning signal. Project page: https://tsuki0512.github.io/AVC-Reward.github.io/

title: Not Just a Subject: Capturing Adaptive Scene-Specific Variance for Visual Storytelling
abstract: Recent advancements in diffusion models have significantly improved text-to-image generation, enabling their application to visual storytelling, where coherent image sequences are generated from narrative prompts. However, existing methods primarily focus on identity preservation and often fail to adapt to diverse scene variations, resulting in semantic misalignment and structural inflexibility. We propose EOS-Story, a training-free framework that harmonizes identity consistency with scene-specific adaptation across text and vision spaces. In the text space, we decouple the narrative into identity and scene sub-prompts to prevent information dilution, but this leaves the scene without access to appearance cues. To bridge this gap, we introduce Cross-Contextual Bridging, which softly injects a phrase-level appearance residual into the scene's <EOS> embedding. In the vision space, we find that scale mismatch between identity and scene subjects causes a few identity tokens to be repeatedly transferred, producing structural artifacts. We address this with Adaptive Identity Preservation, which anchors identity features at the scene-specific scale (Identity Anchoring) and integrates them via Identity-Aware Self-Attention. To evaluate performance under varied spatial compositions, we extend the Consistory+ benchmark with diverse framing scenarios (Consistory+_+). Extensive experiments show that EOS-Story achieves competitive or superior performance on both benchmarks.

title: Velox: Spatial Memory Makes World Models Efficient
abstract: Video world models turn actions and camera motion into long visual rollouts, making video a natural interface for interactive simulation. Such interaction requires responsive generation, yet coherent rollouts must retain visual memory of what has already been generated. Chunked video diffusion models usually keep this context in growing KV caches, so later chunks become progressively slower. To address this bottleneck, we introduce Velox, a training-free attention router for region-level context selection using frustum slab correspondences from streaming geometry. Velox represents historical blocks as camera frustum slabs with depth intervals and obtains current-block depth through recency-priority multiwarp. For well-covered regions, frustum slab overlap softly modulates each layer's model-derived block importance. Uncovered regions retain the model-derived route without geometric bias. The fixed token-block granularity matches FlashAttention-style tiled execution and reduces the attention term that grows with rollout length. Frustum slab construction runs asynchronously with denoising on the same H200. At chunk 48, Velox accelerates attention by $4.36\times$ and denoising by $2.43\times$. On the full 158-case WBench navigation split, it remains within 0.15 API-free average points of dense LingBot-Fast-Cam. Please see our project page at https://velox-world.com/velox/ for more details.

title: ARC-SORT: Adaptive, Robust, Compensated Multi-Object Tracking with Interacting Multiple Models
abstract: Multi-object tracking in sports broadcasts is hard for two reasons: athletes move fast and change direction abruptly, and the camera pans and zooms at the same time. We present ARC-SORT (Adaptive, Robust, Compensated SORT), a tracking-by-detection tracker that trains nothing and runs in real time. Its design rule: the tracker measures its own uncertainty, and that measurement decides how it acts. An Interacting Multiple Model (IMM) Kalman filter gives every track a predictive covariance, and we turn it into a per-track search region: the less reliable the motion prediction, the larger the region in which a detection may match (uncertainty-adaptive Expansion IoU, EIoU). On identical inputs, this continuous coupling is what matters: the same covariance used as a hard Mahalanobis gate hurts at every threshold we swept, and richer covariance summaries add nothing measurable. When two tracks cross, the assignment cost itself reports whether the decision was close. ARC-SORT keeps such pairs under review and applies at most one corrective identity swap once post-crossing appearance evidence shows the first decision was wrong; this adds +1.0 HOTA (higher order tracking accuracy) on both the SportsMOT and DanceTrack test sets at under a millisecond per frame. For players who leave the frame for seconds, motion extrapolation carries no information, so our offline re-identification drops the usual motion gate and links tracklets by appearance alone. ARC-SORT reaches 81.82 HOTA on the SportsMOT test set with the fewest identity switches of the 69 leaderboard entries as of August 2026 and tied-third multi-object tracking accuracy (MOTA, 97.09), and 62.1 HOTA on DanceTrack test with the same association settings. On Deep-EIoU's public detections and embeddings it reaches 80.31 HOTA, +3.1 over Deep-EIoU. It runs at about 50 frames per second on a laptop RTX 3060 GPU. Code will be released.

title: Grounded Human-Attributed Description and Activity Recognition in Videos
abstract: Understanding characteristics and activities of individuals in complex multi-person environments is crucial for real-world applications. However, existing datasets often simplify this problem to grounded group activity recognition, single-person activity recognition, or close-set activity recognition, thus limiting the generalizability of models trained on these datasets. In this work, we introduce the task of Grounded Human-Attributed Description and Activity Recognition (GHADAR), which involves describing the characteristics and activity descriptions of \textbf{every} person in a video, provided the location of the person in the video, which is more practical for real-world applications. To facilitate this, we introduce a new dataset derived from AVA-Actions by generating open-set captions for the person description and activity. In addition, we propose a novel method to effectively utilize the information contained in grounding during training by constraining the cross-attention masks during training in VLMs to improve performance for this task. Our experiments show that our method outperforms SOTA VLMs on this task. Finally, we demonstrate the limitations of existing evaluation metrics, which are overly reliant on human-annotations and exact text-text matching. As an added video-based evaluation, we propose a holistic VLM-based evaluation schema that compares concepts {\em directly} between the video and the generated predictions. Thus, in this work, we develop a complete framework for GHADAR, including a dataset, a novel method and an evaluation schema, thereby establishing a strong foundation for future research in this domain.

title: Routing Policy Optimization for Online Diffusion Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning can align visual generators with reward signals beyond their pretraining objectives, but existing score-function methods typically introduce stochasticity by perturbing the reverse denoising trajectory, leading to costly rollout-based optimization. We instead ask whether stochastic exploration can be introduced inside the generator while preserving its original sampler. Routing Policy Optimization (RPO) answers this question by turning attention routing into a stochastic exploration action. At a few selected denoising levels, each query block keeps its own block and samples further key blocks in proportion to the generator's native attention mass, or keeps dense attention. The sampled route perturbs the velocity of that transition, and a Gaussian likelihood around the dense velocity scores the perturbation with a score-function objective. RPO further uses a controlled two-rollout estimator: two rollouts share the same prompt, initial latent, routed denoising levels, and dense anchor layers, differing only in their sampled attention routes. Their reward difference provides an advantage signal for the routed transitions. Because the likelihood differentiates the dense velocity itself, the learned updates remain effective after routing is removed. At inference, RPO restores dense attention and retains the original deterministic sampler. Experiments on text-to-image and text-to-video generation show that RPO improves generation quality while achieving nearly 4x higher training efficiency than Flow-GRPO-style methods. Please see our project page at https://velox-world.com/rpo for visual results.

title: MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Native Attention Matching
abstract: Spatial intelligence lets an agent perceive and act in the physical world, and many of its judgments must be made at interaction rates: which spatial relation holds, how far an object is, or where to place it. Vision-language models (VLMs) produce these answers by free-form text generation, paying for autoregressive decoding and answer parsing even though the output space is compact: one of a few options, a scalar, or a 2D point. In light of this, we introduce MJev-Spatial, a System 1 multimodal decision model that tackles all three types of spatial understanding tasks within a unified classification framework. Specifically, MJev-Spatial treats each candidate as a class and scores it using the backbone's pretrained query and key projections, without adding parameters. The candidates are the given options for choice tasks, or value bins and image regions refined through coarse-to-fine classification for numerical and point prediction, respectively. At inference, each classification decision takes a single forward pass and generates no answer tokens. To train on heterogeneous spatial data efficiently, we supervise all coarse-to-fine stages jointly with teacher forcing in one forward pass, and combine this with length-aware global batching and cross-GPU load balancing, raising training throughput by 30.8% over the original batching strategy. Built on Qwen3.5-4B and trained on 12.3M question-answer pairs converted from existing spatial datasets, MJev-Spatial achieves the highest overall score (65.64%) among eight tested models, ranks first on seven of twelve benchmarks, and outperforms its unmodified autoregressive base model on all twelve, while running 2.5 times faster than the fastest autoregressive baseline and 5.6 times faster than the base model.

title: Beyond Pairwise Repulsion: Collective Diversity via Determinant Maximization in Diffusion Sampling
abstract: Strong guidance in text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models concentrates sampling toward high-density modes of the conditional distribution, collapsing independently sampled noise vectors onto nearly identical visual prototypes. This limits utility for tasks that demand distributional breadth, most critically synthetic data augmentation. Diversity, however, is a collective property of the whole batch: a set can preserve every pairwise distance yet still collapse onto a low-dimensional subspace. Existing sum-of-pairwise noise-optimization and repulsion objectives respond only weakly to this higher-order failure. We propose DetNO (Determinant Noise Optimization), which formulates diverse generation as RKHS volume maximization on the initial noise, maximizing the log-determinant of an RBF Gram matrix over one-step Tweedie predictions. This set-level functional equals the squared batch volume; its repulsion is strongest when the batch is most collapsed and self-attenuates as diversity is achieved. An anchor-based fidelity term keeps the optimized noises near plausible regions, and Lagrangian relaxation gives a two-term objective with a single hyperparameter $λ$ governing the diversity-quality trade-off, without training or sampler modification. Across three backbones (SD1.5, SDXL, SD3), DetNO achieves leading intra-batch diversity in VendiScore and Mean Self-Similarity, and a downstream few-shot classification experiment confirms that broader mode coverage brings statistically significant accuracy gains for synthetic data augmentation in the low-shot regime.
